title: Two Coworkers Talk About Bilal's Steadfastness
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Fajar, I read something last night that I can't stop thinking about, about a companion named Bilal.
Fajar: [curious] Bilal ibn Rabah? The one who gave the very first call to prayer?
Dewi: [nodding] Yes, but before that, his life was incredibly hard. He was enslaved in Makkah when he accepted Islam.
Fajar: [sadly] I remember hearing that his enslaver punished him badly for changing his faith.
Dewi: [tense] Terribly. He was dragged into the desert, and a heavy stone was placed on his chest under the burning sun.
Fajar: [wincing] That's horrifying to even imagine. What did they want from him?
Dewi: [reflective] They wanted him to reject his faith and worship their idols instead, just to stop the pain.
Fajar: [quietly] Did he give in, under all that suffering?
Dewi: [with wonder] Never. He just kept repeating one word, over and over, 'Ahad, Ahad,' meaning One God.
Fajar: [amazed] Even while in that much pain, his mind stayed completely focused on that single truth.
Dewi: [warmly] Eventually, Abu Bakr heard about his suffering and paid to purchase his freedom immediately.
Fajar: [relieved] That must have felt like an enormous turning point in Bilal's whole life.
Dewi: [smiling] It truly was. And later, the Prophet chose Bilal to give the adhan, the call to prayer, because of his beautiful voice.
Fajar: [thoughtful] From enslaved man to the very first voice calling people to prayer. That's remarkable.
Dewi: [reflective] What stays with me most is how his heart was already free, long before his body ever was.
Fajar: [nodding] That's a powerful way to think about it. Freedom starting on the inside, not the outside.
Dewi: [warmly] Exactly. Whenever I feel stuck in a hard situation now, I think about Bilal under that stone.
Fajar: [smiling] I think I'll remember his story too, especially on days when patience feels difficult.

quiz.question: What was Bilal's situation in Makkah before his freedom?
options: He was an enslaved man who accepted Islam
quiz.explanation: Dewi explains he was enslaved in Makkah when he accepted Islam.

He was sent away from Makkah

quiz.explanation: Abu Bakr heard about his suffering and paid to purchase his freedom.
